title: Paternal grandparents in Natalbany, Louisiana
summary: Lee recalls his grandfather the blacksmith and grandmother the evangelist on a farm near Hammond, Louisiana.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Can you trace your family back further than your own parents? Your own father?

No, I can't. Yeah, wait a second now. Okay ... gee, this is tough. There was a time when; it seems I remember when I was 3 or 4 -- I don't think I was even 5 years old that I'm talking about now, that I remember my grandmother, you know. My grandfather was a blacksmith, okay, and my grandmother was an Evangelist.

Yes, my father's mother, you know, she was an Evangelist, and my grandfather was a blacksmith, because my daddy used to talk about how hard he used to work so he could go to college, you know, and my grandmother --I just remember her -- I think maybe I saw her once or twice, in a place called Natalbany (PHONETIC) Louisiana, if that's the way you pronounce that. I understand that's not 100 miles from New Orleans -- but all I can remember, it sounds like to me it was called Natalbany where they just had a store -- you know how in the small towns where they just have a commissary or whatever they call them. That's all they had, was just the one store where you bought everything; you know, all of your supplies for whatever.
But my auntie and my uncle and my grandmother and
Do you know how to spell the name of that town?
No. I can't even pronounce it! It's probably wrong.
Well, we'll look it up. What were their names?

Well, I'll tell you what it was near. It was near Hammond, Louisiana - Natallbany was right next to Hammond, and I know how to spell Hammond. I don't really know, though, because I, like, visit them from New Orleans to Natallbenny, and I went back, but I don't remember -- I just recall seeing them once or twice. They had a farm; they lived on a farm, you know.
